concept: Form is the case that holds a unit's fields and sends them. When a send fails it does what a device does when a setting is out of range: one window at the top counts the problems and names each one, and every name takes you to the field. Nothing is sent until every field is right.

default_to_avoid.pattern: form that validates on every keystroke from the first character and shows red inline errors with no summary, or a toast that says there are errors
default_to_avoid.why_not: The person is scolded before they finish typing, and a toast leaves no way to find which field is wrong, so the form must count the problems in one window and link each to its field.

default_to_avoid.pattern: form built on a form library with a controller around every field
default_to_avoid.why_not: It forces every control through a wrapper and a store, while a native form already holds the values and the validity of each field, so Form reads them from the DOM.

references.source: system/FORM.md display class: a window recessed into the body that says the state, in numbers or a few words
Braun ET 66 calculator (Dietrich Lubs, 1987): the window shows the figure and a printed key names what to press next
GOV.UK Design System error summary: a titled list at the top of the page that links to each field and takes focus

derivation.consequence: the window is recessed into the body (inverse light)
derivation.form: The error summary is a window with surface.sunken and elevation.well, so it reads as the unit's reading of what is wrong and never as a raised card.

derivation.consequence: tabular figures everywhere a number changes
derivation.form: The count of problems prints in tabular figures at the emphasis size, before the words, so the number is the first thing read and does not shift as it falls.

derivation.consequence: every mechanism has its keyboard map
derivation.form: Enter in a field sends, a failed send puts focus on the window, Tab walks the links, and Enter on a link puts focus in the field it names.

derivation.consequence: orange appears once per unit, on the primary control's body only
derivation.form: The submit key is the unit's one Button of kind primary, and the summary, the links and the busy state use ink only.

derivation.consequence: no entry choreography, no idle animation
derivation.form: The summary appears and its rows leave at once with no slide or fade, and the sending state changes a word and the key's height, not a spinner.

options.name: recessed window with the count first
raised strip with a bullet list

variants.reason: B uses the recessed window that Input and Stepper already use for a reading, and the count leads like a figure on a display; A is a hairline box that has no body of its own and reads as a Fieldset, and C is a raised part that looks like a button or the Banner.

root.why: A native form with one column and a fixed gap, so the summary, the fields and the keys stand on the same inset line.

summary.why: The window that reports the failed send is recessed with the inverse light and takes focus when the send fails, so it is read before anything else.

summaryTitle.why: The window's heading names the group of problems in the emphasis size and medium weight, and aria-labelledby makes it the group's accessible name.

count.why: The count is a number that changes as problems are fixed, so it prints in tabular figures and does not move the words beside it.

list.why: The problems are a list in field order, so the screen reader reads how many there are and the Tab key walks them in the order of the form.

item.why: Each row holds the link and its message in one column with a hairline above it, like a printed table of readings.

link.why: The field's name is a link, a row at least as tall as a key, and pressing it puts the focus in the field so the person can fix it at once.

message.why: The message says what is wrong in secondary ink under the link, at more than 4.5:1 on the recessed plastic.

submit.why: The submit key wraps the unit's one primary Button and stops sending while a send runs, so a second press cannot send twice.

aria-disabled=true.why: While a send runs the submit key loses its height and fades, flat on the body, and the word changes to Sending, so the state is not told by colour.

hover.why: A summary link thickens its rule under the pointer and nothing lifts, because a printed word does not rise when you approach it.

active.why: A press on the submit key while it is sending moves nothing, so the held key reads as flat and not as pressed.

focus.why: The window shows the dark ring whenever the form puts focus on it after a failed send, whether the key or a pointer sent it.

focus-visible.why: The window and each link show the same dark ring as every part when they hold the keyboard focus.

@media forced-colors: active.why: In forced colours the summary keeps a real border and its links use the system link colour.
